subject: Science
stem: The thinning of the protective atmospheric layer that shields Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation, caused mainly by chemicals like CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) once used in refrigerants and aerosols, is called:
explanation: Ozone layer depletion (linked to CFCs) thins the stratospheric ozone that blocks harmful UV radiation — a distinct environmental issue from global warming (greenhouse gas-driven temperature rise), though both are human-caused atmospheric problems.
